small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_SP to 64 or 128 and BLOCK_OC to 32; current 16×16 tiles underutilize tensor cores and launch too many SP iterations (4096 outputs / 16 = 256 inner loops per program). Sweep (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP, IC_BLOCK) ∈ {(32,64,32),(64,64,16),(32,128,16)} with num_warps=4 or 8, num_stages=2.
- The current loop redundantly loads each input position 4 times (once per (ii,jj)); restructure to load each input tile once per (kh,kw) and accumulate into the four c_ij from the same x_vals — this cuts input traffic ~4×.
- Increase the grid: launch (N, cdiv(OC,BLOCK_OC), cdiv(H_pool*W_pool,BLOCK_SP)) and do a final atomic-add (or two-stage reduction) to combine spatial partials, exposing far more parallelism than the current N*cdiv(OC,16)=128*4=512 programs.
large_guidance:
- Since stride=1, padding=1, k=3, ConvTranspose2d ≡ Conv2d with flipped weight (same H,W output). Treat the problem as: per (n, oc), compute a reduction over all H*W output pixels of hardtanh(maxpool2x2(conv3x3))/area, then tanh. Make the kernel persistent per (n, oc_tile): stream over H_pool*W_pool tiles with a large BLOCK_SP, accumulate into a scalar per oc, and store after tanh — eliminating the output write of the full feature map entirely.
- Use an im2col-style GEMM formulation: form K=IC*9 reduction; for each output spatial tile load the 9 shifted IC slabs once and do a single tl.dot of shape [BLOCK_OC, K] x [K, BLOCK_SP] instead of 9 separate dots and 4 redundant input loads. Keep NHWC layout so the IC axis is contiguous for the K-dim load.
- Alternatively, split into two kernels: (1) a tuned conv3x3 GEMM (im2col implicit) writing the post-conv feature map in NHWC, (2) a fused maxpool+hardtanh+mean+tanh reduction kernel. The reduction is cheap; the conv dominates and benefits from being a clean GEMM with autotuned BLOCK_M/N/K rather than a hand-rolled 9-dot loop.
